dimensions.note: Re-read after adding the HTML report. It renders only fields already in the candidates document; no secrets, emails or names are read or written. The page loads nothing from the network.

Domain rules, both reports and every method are unit tested with a stub registry. New tests cover the HTML report: the count in the title, blockers, escaping of an extension name, the ready track segment and the empty case; the report method test checks that both files are written. The page was also rendered in a browser and looked at. The real swampRegistry (Deno.Command) is still not unit tested; a live smoke test covered it earlier.
refresh skips an extension that already has a reading on the same UTC day (tested), so a rerun is safe.
report now returns two data handles (report and reportHtml). The weekly workflow only calls the method, so it needs no change; the report markdown file is unchanged.
The new reportHtml file spec has infinite lifetime and keeps 52 versions, like the markdown report.

Re-read the new HTML output: every stored string (extension name, steward, blockers, flags, timestamp) goes through escapeHtml, and the rest is numbers and fixed stage names. The page is one file with inline CSS and an inline SVG, no scripts and no external requests. It copies the look of the public Capture repo, not its code. Earlier notes still hold: the _registry test hook cannot be supplied from a CLI input; the README pulls the extension first, covered by a test; subprocess use is documented.

Inputs are typed. _registry is z.any by design (test hook). record, advance and untrack do not regex-check extension, but must find it in the store; by reading the code, a prototype key such as __proto__ gets past that lookup and has no effect on stored data, because it does not survive serialisation. Not covered by a test.
track, record, refresh, advance, untrack and report are present and tested. untrack removes from the latest document; older stored versions keep history.
2026.11.09.1 adds a file spec and no change to globalArguments or the candidates schema, so it carries a no-op upgrade, covered by the existing test that requires an entry for the current version.
